questions.q: Which US forms do you file for someone living in Canada?
questions.a: Commonly Form 1040 along with Forms 2555, 1116, 8938, 8621 and 8833, plus FinCEN Report 114 for the FBAR. A non-resident files Form 1040NR, and Form 8233 covers an exemption from withholding on personal services income.

questions.q: Do I have to pay tax in both the US and Canada?
questions.a: Usually yes, and a Canadian resident who is a US citizen files with both the IRS and the CRA. Tax treaties and the foreign tax credit are what relieve the double tax, and the credit cannot exceed the tax paid in the other country.

questions.q: Is a TFSA tax-free to the IRS?
questions.a: No. The IRS does not treat a TFSA as tax-free, so the income is taxable in the current year and reported on Form 1040. An RRSP is the equivalent of a traditional IRA, and a 401k and an RRSP both defer tax but differ on early withdrawal penalties and rollovers.

questions.q: Who has to report under FATCA?
questions.a: US taxpayers whose foreign assets pass the $50,000 threshold, reported on Form 8938.

questions.q: How does Canadian departure tax work?
questions.a: It turns on whether you have ceased to be a resident, which exemptions apply and the type of asset involved. Rental property, mutual funds, TFSAs and RRSPs are each treated differently when you move to the US, so we work it through case by case.

questions.q: Does the FBAR apply to a company?
questions.a: Yes. It applies to corporations, LLCs, partnerships, trusts and estates, and covers checking and savings accounts, securities and brokerage accounts and other financial institution accounts.

questions.q: Do IRS rules for crypto keep changing?
questions.a: Yes. IRS rules and tax laws are rapidly evolving to catch up with blockchain finance technology, and our experts track those obligations as they change.

questions.q: How does the IRS treat cryptocurrency?
questions.a: As property. A gain on a coin that has risen in price is a taxable capital event in the same way as a physical asset, and a coin held for more than a year qualifies for the long-term rates of 0, 15 or 20 percent.

questions.q: What do you need to work out a year of trading?
questions.a: All of your wallet and exchange data. Connecting your wallets to coin tracking software such as Koinly or CoinTracking records the cost basis of every transaction, and we reconcile deposits, withdrawals and income from there. We do not have a favourite platform and will work in whichever one you use.

questions.q: Is staking or mining income taxed like a trade?
questions.a: No. Staking, yield and mining come in as ordinary income at fair market value on the day you receive them, and the capital gain is worked out from that point. Mining also brings self-employment tax and hardware write-offs.

questions.q: Are NFTs taxed the same as other crypto?
questions.a: Not always. An NFT may be treated as a collectible, which carries a different capital gains rate, so we look at them separately.

questions.q: Is swapping one token for a wrapped version a taxable event?
questions.a: Yes. Converting ETH to wrapped ETH qualifies as a taxable event under IRS rules, and gas fees may be deductible where the activity is structured as an LLC.

about.title: Your partners in business success.
text: We founded Akif CPA after working in large, top-level accounting firms with the goal of helping small and mid-sized businesses succeed. We are a team of highly skilled tax professionals with years of experience in tax, accounting, business advisory, payroll, business consulting, compilation and review services, sales tax audit and financial planning.

Our goal is to exceed our clients' expectations by providing exceptional quality services. We thrive when we help your business grow, and our philosophy centers on our clients' success. That commitment has helped us maintain a strong and diverse portfolio of clients covering many industries and business areas.

Our relationship-based approach transcends the traditional CPA role, where we strive at all times to do what is in the best interest of our clients. Our team of expert CPAs is based primarily in Houston and Toronto.

facts.heading: S-Corp reasonable compensation report
facts.text: A customized report that establishes a defensible compensation amount for an S-Corp owner and protects against an IRS audit. It is set out in six sections - your money, your business, your time, the methodology, the calculations and the considerations - and is built from IRS criteria and court rulings, Bureau of Labor Statistics reports, geographic wage data and our own wage database. You complete a survey about the business and the analysis is tailored to it.
